detailed_rationale:
Adani Power is India's largest private thermal generator at 18,150 MW operating capacity (~7.3% of the country's coal-based generation), with 95% of that capacity locked under long/medium-term PPAs and a further 13.3 GW (56%) of a targeted 23.7 GW expansion pipeline already tied up as of Q4 FY26 (quarter ended March 2026, reported April 2026). Headline numbers look strong: consolidated Q4 FY26 PAT of Rs 4,271 cr (+64% YoY) and FY26 PAT of Rs 12,971 cr (+1.7% YoY over FY25's Rs 12,750 cr). But the earnings-quality picture underneath is weaker than the headline. Continuing (ex-prior-period) revenue for FY26 actually fell to Rs 55,583 cr from Rs 56,473 cr (-1.6%), and continuing EBITDA fell to Rs 21,285 cr from Rs 21,575 cr (-1.3%) - the core business shrank in FY26. What bridged that to a modestly positive PAT print was (a) Rs 2,283 cr of prior-period/regulatory true-up revenue recognized during the year (Rs 930 cr of it in Q4 alone, versus just Rs 13 cr in Q4 FY25 - this is what drove reported Q4 EBITDA growth to 27% versus continuing EBITDA growth of only 9.3%), and (b) a lower tax charge, which the company itself cited as the primary driver of the 64% Q4 PAT jump (a legacy of the FY24 deferred-tax-asset recognition that keeps effective tax rates depressed). Full-year PLF also fell to 66.5% from 70.5% (recovering to 74% only in Q4), and merchant/spot power realizations compressed - IEX average clearing price was down 12.4% YoY to Rs 3.88/kWh in Q4, and full-year DAM tariffs fell from Rs 4.4 to Rs 3.8/unit - a real headwind on the ~21% of FY26 sales volume (20.9 of 99.15 BU) that is merchant-exposed, even though 95% of capacity is nominally PPA-backed. Q1 FY27 results are not out yet: board meeting is scheduled 22-Jul-2026 with the investor call on 23-Jul-2026.

On the balance sheet, total debt jumped to Rs 53,556 cr (March 2026) from Rs 38,335 cr a year earlier (+40%), net debt to Rs 45,022 cr from Rs 31,023 cr (+45%), funding a Rs 2 lakh crore, 23.7 GW capacity build-out (targeting ~41.9 GW total by FY32) of which the largest single projects (Raipur Phase-II 54% complete, Raigarh Phase-II 47% complete) are still years from full contribution; only Mahan Phase-II (86%) is near completion. ICRA (AA/Stable, A1+, April 2026, on Rs 69,000 cr of facilities) and CARE (January 2026) both reaffirmed strong ratings, citing the PPA-backed revenue visibility on the existing ~18 GW fleet (~90% contracted as of Sep-2025; promoter holding 74.96% at that date, no fresh pledge data located this pass), but this is a business levering up materially ahead of earnings delivery, in a year where India's own power-demand growth came in at just 0.8% (a multi-year low) and national thermal PLF slid to 65-66% on renewables share gains - a genuine cyclical headwind management is counting on reversing (FY27 industry demand growth guided at 5-5.5%) but hasn't yet delivered. Adani Power also carries a recurring single-buyer receivable risk at its Godda (Bangladesh-dedicated) plant: after a 2024 arrears crisis that peaked near $845m and was only resolved via a $437m one-time payment plus a two-month LC and sovereign guarantee in mid-2025, a fresh $112.7m payment demand surfaced in January 2026 - a reminder that a chunk of earnings sits with a single, politically fragile counterparty.

Governance is cleaner than the 2023 Hindenburg period but not fully closed: SEBI's September 2025 final orders found no LODR violations in the specific transactions probed, but SEBI has not published a comprehensive report and more than a dozen related cases remain pending, and a February 2026 OCCRP report resurfaced ~$3bn of Adani-family-associate investment via offshore hedge funds - group-level noise that periodically hits all Adani-listed names including this one. On valuation: the stock trades at ~32-37x trailing consolidated earnings (price ~Rs 214, market cap ~Rs 4.14 lakh cr as of mid-July 2026), up ~81% over 12 months to a 52-week high, with sell-side (Jefferies, June 2026, target Rs 255) explicitly modeling a 23% EBITDA CAGR through FY26-29E to justify a 20x FY28E EV/EBITDA multiple. That is a materially higher growth path than the FY26 print supports - continuing EBITDA just declined 1.3% - and depends on flawless, on-time delivery of a debt-funded, multi-GW brownfield capex program plus a demand-cycle reacceleration that hasn't shown up in the numbers yet.
recommendation_rationale: Sell, not Hold, because the gap between price and demonstrated earnings power is too wide to underwrite passively. A 32-37x trailing multiple - already re-rated ~80% in a year to a 52-week high - is being justified by sell-side models assuming 20%+ forward EBITDA CAGR, while the FY26 print that should be the growth base actually shows continuing EBITDA down 1.3% and continuing revenue down 1.6%, with essentially all of the reported PAT growth traceable to one-off prior-period regulatory income (Rs 2,283 cr for the year) and a depressed tax rate rather than volume/tariff-led operating momentum. Layer on debt +40% YoY funding a still-early-stage capex program (largest new units 47-86% complete), a soft national demand cycle, merchant-tariff deflation on the ~21% of volumes that are spot-exposed, a recurring Bangladesh receivable problem, and residual group-governance noise - and the risk-reward tilts toward de-risking rather than holding through the re-rating. This is not a Hold-vs-Sell coin-flip: the earnings-quality dissection (one-offs bridging an otherwise-shrinking base) is a clear, sourced finding, not a close call.
summary: Adani Power had a strong-looking FY26 on the surface - profit up modestly for the year and up 64% in the final quarter - but a large part of that came from one-time regulatory income recognition and a lower tax bill, not from the underlying power business, which actually shrank slightly (revenue and operating profit both down about 1-2% year-on-year) as India's electricity-demand growth slowed sharply and spot power prices fell. The company is now borrowing heavily (debt up 40% in a year) to fund a large, multi-year plant-expansion plan that is still early in construction, and it continues to face periodic payment delays from its Bangladesh power customer. With the stock near a 52-week high and trading at a rich 32-37 times earnings - pricing in a much stronger growth path than the latest results actually show - we would use strength to reduce exposure rather than add or hold through the current valuation.
positive_para: The bull case is real, not just hype: Adani Power is the largest private thermal generator in India with 95% of its current ~18 GW fleet locked under long/medium-term PPAs, giving unusually strong revenue visibility for a commodity power business, and credit-rating agencies (ICRA AA/Stable, CARE) reaffirmed strong ratings as recently as April 2026. Management has already tied up 13.3 GW (56%) of its targeted 23.7 GW capacity expansion under fresh PPAs (including a new 1,600 MW, 25-year Maharashtra award and a 558 MW Tamil Nadu award in Q4 alone), and execution on prior projects has been credible - Mahan Phase-II is 86% complete. If India's power-demand growth reaccelerates to the 5-5.5% industry guidance for FY27 as management expects, plant-load factors recover further from the Q4 FY26 print of 74%, and the balance sheet doesn't over-lever before the new capacity starts contributing, the absolute earnings base by FY29-30 could genuinely be much larger than today - the growth runway is not fictional, just not yet fully delivered.
negative_para: The strongest bear point is earnings quality: strip out the Rs 2,283 cr of prior-period/regulatory true-up income recognized in FY26 (Rs 930 cr of it in Q4 alone) and the lower tax charge that management itself flagged as the main driver of the 64% Q4 PAT jump, and the underlying business actually contracted - continuing revenue and continuing EBITDA both declined roughly 1-2% year-on-year in FY26, with full-year PLF down to 66.5% from 70.5%. That contraction happened in a year when India's overall power-demand growth was just 0.8% (a multi-year low) and national thermal PLF fell to 65-66% as renewables took share - a cyclical backdrop management is betting will reverse but hasn't yet. Meanwhile the balance sheet is levering up fast (total debt +40% YoY to Rs 53,556 cr) to fund a capex program whose largest new units are only 47-86% built, the Godda (Bangladesh) plant keeps generating fresh single-buyer payment disputes (a $112.7m demand letter in January 2026, barely a year after an $845m arrears crisis was resolved), and unresolved group-level governance questions (OCCRP's February 2026 report on ~$3bn of associate-linked offshore investment, SEBI's still-pending dozen-plus cases) remain a background risk. None of that squares with a stock at 32-37x trailing earnings, up 80% in a year to a 52-week high, priced for 20%+ sustained EBITDA growth.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At ~32-37x trailing consolidated PE and a price near its 52-week high, the market (and sell-side models like Jefferies' June-2026 target of Rs 255, which explicitly assumes 23% EBITDA CAGR FY26-29E to back a 20x FY28E EV/EBITDA multiple) is pricing sustained 20%+ per-annum EBITDA growth for several years. The FY26 print that should be the launch pad for that growth instead shows continuing EBITDA down 1.3% and continuing revenue down 1.6% YoY, with reported profit growth manufactured almost entirely by one-off prior-period regulatory income and a depressed tax rate. My own forward 3-5y view is roughly 12% (capacity is genuinely set to grow from 18.15 GW to a targeted ~41.9 GW by FY32, a plausible low-teens CAGR, but tempered by: only 56% of the new capacity is PPA-tied so far, the largest new units are still 47-86% complete with years of execution risk ahead, national power-demand growth just posted its weakest year in some time, and ~21% of current sales volume remains merchant-exposed into a falling spot-tariff market). A stock priced for ~20%+ against a business I can genuinely underwrite at ~12% is rich - this is a direct read of the FY26 continuing-operations numbers against the multiple, not a base-effect argument. Verdict: rich, not cheap or fair.

technical_commentary: A genuinely violent history -- an early 4x run, a 65% single-episode crash (2023, group-crisis era), then an 8x recovery to a new all-time high of Rs254 in May-2026 -- means the multi-year chart is directional but scarred, not smooth. The most recent leg (Rs140 to Rs243 in two months) is parabolic; volume did expand into it, arguing real participation rather than pure distribution, but a vertical move like this is also classically extended and due a real consolidation. MA stack is fully bullish and widely separated; score nets the strong trend against extension risk.
